body:
auth.require_account() runs `UPDATE auth_tokens SET last_seen_at = ?` plus a
COMMIT on every single authenticated request — including every /sync poll from
every device. On a WAL SQLite database on an SD-card-backed host (this deploy
target) that is a durable write per request for a value whose only consumer is
the sessions list in Settings, where minute-level precision is meaningless.

Fix: only touch last_seen_at when it is actually stale — e.g. skip the UPDATE
unless now - last_seen_at > 15 min (one line: fetch last_seen_at in the
existing SELECT, compare before writing). Keeps the sessions screen just as
useful, drops ~all of the per-request write load. Alternatively defer the
commit into the request's existing transaction where one exists — but the
staleness check is simpler and enough.

Files: server/src/shoppinglist_server/auth.py, server/tests/test_auth.py.
title: Server: last_seen_at write + commit on every authed request — throttle to staleness
